Index of the documentation for Tabchat.

Updated 2026-10-13 · Source README.md

Tabchat documentation

A native macOS app that brings WhatsApp, Discord, Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, Brightspace and any website into one window via a sidebar of service icons, all sharing the system's own web engine (WKWebView). Rewritten from scratch in Swift, macOS 14+, Apple Silicon only, targeting users who want a single native app instead of bouncing between browsers and standalone clients.

Status: design and early implementation. Early phases (Engine spike, Skeleton) are complete; Core integration is underway. See TASKS.md at the project root for current status.

Terms used throughout

Term Meaning
WKWebView The system WebKit browser engine (same as Safari); used by Tabchat to display services
Service A web app or website (WhatsApp, Discord, Teams, etc.) shown in a sidebar tab
Tab One instance of a service; the app can have multiple tabs of the same service (e.g. two WhatsApp accounts)
Profile A WKWebsiteDataStore for one sign-in; shared by related services (e.g. Teams, Outlook, OneDrive via "microsoft-work")
Unread A count badge on a service tab, the Dock icon and menu bar
Focus macOS notification Focus modes; Tabchat respects them before showing notifications

What Tabchat is, the ideas behind it, and what is in and out of scope.

Updated 2026-10-13 · Source 01-overview.md · Read first: Tabchat documentation

Overview

What it is

Tabchat is a native macOS app that brings messaging and productivity services—WhatsApp, Discord, Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, Brightspace, and any website—into one window. Services appear as icons in a sidebar; each can have multiple accounts (e.g., two WhatsApp numbers) with separate sign-ins, except Teams/Outlook/OneDrive which share one Microsoft login.

The app reuses the system's WebKit engine (WKWebView), so it stays lightweight and integrates deeply with macOS: unread badges on the Dock icon and menu bar, native notifications that respect Focus modes, menu bar icon for always-at-hand access, start-at-login support.

Credit: Tabchat is a rewrite from scratch of MMV2408/tabchat, an Electron app for Linux (MIT License, © Mike Vijverberg). This fork is macOS-only; the original Linux code lives on the Linux branch (tag upstream-final).

The ideas behind it

  1. One app, not context-switching: Bring all your messaging and work apps into one place instead of Alt-Tab between browsers and standalone apps.
  2. Native and lightweight: Built in Swift with macOS system frameworks (SwiftUI, AppKit, WKWebView), not a bundled browser. The app itself is a few megabytes; all the heavy lifting is the web service.
  3. Unified notifications: Notifications arrive in one place, respect your Focus modes, and clicking one opens the right service in the window instead of a new window or tab.
  4. Deep macOS integration: The app lives in the menu bar when closed, updates Dock and menu bar badges, supports start-at-login via SMAppService, uses system theme (light/dark).

Scope: v1 features

  • Sidebar of service icons, icon badges for unread
  • Services: WhatsApp, Discord, Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, Brightspace, custom sites
  • Multiple accounts per service, each with its own sign-in; Teams, Outlook (work), OneDrive and Brightspace share one Microsoft sign-in by default
  • One WKWebsiteDataStore per sign-in; sign-ins survive restart
  • Unread counts in Dock badge and menu bar dot
  • Native notifications via UNUserNotificationCenter; respects Focus; clicking opens the service
  • Menu bar icon; app closes to menu bar, optional start-at-login
  • Pause notifications (1 hour, until tomorrow 08:00, until off)
  • Find on page, downloads, back/forward/reload/home buttons
  • Light/dark mode following the system

Out of scope (v1)

  • Split view, Cmd+K quick switcher, tab sleep, duplicate/incognito tabs, card reorder/hide
  • Linux packaging, GNOME D-Bus integration
  • Upstream updater, Sparkle, donate/what's new screens

What stays hard

  1. WebRTC in WKWebView on macOS: Teams and Discord calls, and Teams screen share. The engine spike confirmed these work, but edge cases (mute, camera, screen content) may need workarounds.
  2. School SSO for Brightspace: Some institutions use OIDC or SAML flows that might not survive WKWebsiteDataStore boundaries.
  3. Unread detection: Each service reports unread differently—count in tab title (3) …, favicon, or hidden DOM. Hardcoded CSS selectors and JS injection per service.

System components, data flow, and design decisions.

Updated 2026-10-13 · Source 02-architecture.md · Read first: Tabchat documentation, Overview

Architecture

The app is built as a SwiftUI app with AppKit where needed for menu bar and system integration. WKWebView instances are created on demand per tab; the system persists sign-in state in WKWebsiteDataStore objects identified by profile name.

Component tree

TabchatApp (SwiftUI app entry point, menu bar extra, app menu with Cmd shortcuts)
├── Store                    single source of truth: tabs, profiles, settings
│                            persisted as JSON in ~/Library/Application Support/Tabchat
├── Profile                  one WKWebsiteDataStore per sign-in
│                            ("microsoft-work" shared by Teams/Outlook/OneDrive;
│                            "whatsapp-1", "whatsapp-2" separate)
├── TabController            manages one WKWebView per tab; creates on demand, drops on sleep
├── ServiceCatalog           per service: URL, icon, user agent, unread rule
├── Bridge (JavaScript)      user script injected into each tab
│                            • shims window.Notification
│                            • reports unread count to native code via WKScriptMessageHandler
├── Notifier                 UNUserNotificationCenter
│                            • sends native notifications for new messages
│                            • respects macOS Focus modes
│                            • pause timer (1h, until 08:00 tomorrow, until off)
│                            • notification click selects the service and brings window to front
├── Badge                    Dock tile badge (sum of all unread) + menu bar dot indicator
├── Sidebar                  icon + name per tab, drag-reorder, unread count
├── TabView                  WKWebView instance and toolbar (back/forward/reload/home/find/downloads)
└── LoginItem                SMAppService for start-at-login, optional hidden mode

Data flow: opening a tab

  1. User clicks a service in the sidebar.
  2. TabController checks if a WKWebView exists for that profile; if not, creates one.
  3. WKWebView loads the URL for that service, using the profile's WKWebsiteDataStore for cookies and site data.
  4. JavaScript Bridge is injected; it replaces window.Notification with a callback to native code.
  5. User signs in. Cookies and session storage are persisted in the profile's WKWebsiteDataStore.

Data flow: new message notification

  1. Web page script (e.g. Discord) displays a notification via window.Notification("3 new messages").
  2. Injected Bridge script intercepts it and posts to WKScriptMessageHandler.
  3. Notifier receives the message, extracts count, and shows a native UNUserNotification.
  4. User clicks the notification; Notifier selects the service tab and brings the window to front.

Persistence

  • Profiles and tabs: ~/Library/Application Support/Tabchat/state.json holds open tabs, profile names, and user settings (theme, pause state, start-at-login).
  • Sign-in state: Each profile's WKWebsiteDataStore holds cookies, session storage, and site data, persisted by WKWebView.

Planned but not yet built (v2+)

  • Split view (two tabs side by side)
  • Tab sleep: unload a tab's WKWebView after idle time to save memory; reload on next use
  • Duplicate tab, incognito tab
  • Card reorder and hide
  • Cmd+K quick switcher palette

provisionaldevelopers

Requirements, development environment, and build commands.

Updated 2026-10-13 · Source 03-building.md · Read first: Tabchat documentation

Building

Requirements

  • macOS 14 Sonoma or later (to run the app; the app targets macOS 14+)
  • Apple Silicon (M1 or later; Intel not supported)
  • Xcode 26 or later (Swift 6; CI uses 26.6, development uses 27)
  • Homebrew (for build tools)

Development environment

Install build tools:

brew install xcodegen swiftlint swiftformat just

These are used by the build recipes:

  • xcodegen: Generates the Xcode project from project.yml
  • swiftlint: Lints Swift code for style and correctness
  • swiftformat: Auto-formats Swift code
  • just: Task runner (like make, but simpler; recipes in justfile)

Build commands

All commands use just to run recipes defined in justfile. The recipes generate the Xcode project (xcodegen) and then run Xcode commands.

Generate Xcode project

just gen

Generates Tabchat.xcodeproj from project.yml. Run this after any change to project.yml or when syncing from remote.

Build

just build

Builds the app for release (Ad-hoc code signing, no provisioning profile needed for local testing). Output: build/Release/Tabchat.app.

Run

just run

Builds and runs the app in the simulator or on the current Mac.

Test

just test

Runs XCTest unit and integration tests. Tests are in Tests/.

Lint

just lint

Runs swiftlint to check for style and correctness issues. Errors block CI; warnings are logged.

Format

just format

Auto-formats Swift code with swiftformat. Useful before committing.

Release (planned)

just release

Packages the app as a .app and unsigned .dmg in dist/. Later, with Developer ID signing and notarization: a signed, notarized .dmg ready to share.

Development workflow

  1. Clone and install:

    git clone https://github.com/narendranag/tabchat.git
cd tabchat
brew install xcodegen swiftlint swiftformat just

  2. Generate and build:

    just gen
just build

  3. Run locally:

    just run

    or open Tabchat.xcodeproj in Xcode and build from there.

  4. Make changes:

    • Edit Swift code in App/Sources/
    • Add or change tests in Tests/
    • If project.yml changes, run just gen again

  5. Before committing:

    just format
just lint
just test

  6. CI/CD:

    • Push to main or open a PR
    • GitHub Actions runs just lint, just test, just build automatically (see .github/workflows/ci.yml)

Debugging

In Xcode

  1. Open Tabchat.xcodeproj
  2. Set breakpoints in Swift code
  3. Run with Cmd+R or the Play button
  4. Use the Debug navigator and console

App logs

The app logs to the standard system log and to ~/Library/Logs/Tabchat/. View with:

log show --predicate 'process == "Tabchat"' --level debug

Planned (not yet built)

  • Release build with Developer ID signing and notarization
  • Sparkle updates
  • Auto-formatting in CI (optional, on PR review)
